solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Squatter — I must leave truck

indicators.note: the letter named just before must leave the word it is in, so it is taken out

parts.note: squatter is the comparative of squat, meaning more short and stout, so dumpier

explanation.surface: A squatter is told to get out of a lorry he has been living in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squatter' looks like a person occupying a building, but it is the adjective: more squat. 'must leave' takes I out of DUMPIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumper is a tipping lorry used on building sites to carry and dump loads.

clue.text: One induced to get up on tiger? Outcome finally requiring careful handling

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
to induce someone is to lead them, so led
a tiger is a big cat

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is coaxed into climbing on a tiger, an outcome needing care.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to get up' reads the induced one upwards; 'on' simply stacks the pieces, and 'finally' takes only the last letter of Outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicate is fragile and needs to be treated gently.

clue.text: Casting a lot, fisherman tackles huge fish

indicators.note: casting off a lot of the two words means throwing most of their letters away, keeping a short run from inside

explanation.surface: An angler casting repeatedly takes on a huge fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting a lot' reads as the angler at work, but it means discarding most of 'fisherman tackles', leaving the letters that straddle the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The manta is a giant ray, among the largest fish in the sea.

clue.text: Some may understand this character to be a consumer

indicators.note: some speakers say this Greek letter's name so that it is heard like the word for a consumer

parts.note: an eater is one who consumes

explanation.surface: Some might take this person to be a big consumer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the Greek letter's name can be heard as EATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, a written character.

clue.text: Burn boxes turned off platform

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to scald is to burn with hot liquid or steam

indicators.note: a word turned round is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: Someone sets fire to the boxes and then turns away from a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the little word, and 'boxes' encloses it in the burn; 'off' looks like part of the surface phrase 'turned off'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, especially one for builders or for a public execution.

clue.text: Odd evidence people can't settle yet for dogs?

indicators.note: for here has the debt note taken in among the dogs

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs
an IOU is a written note of a debt not yet paid

explanation.surface: Strange: people's unpaid bills are being kept for the dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The debt note is singular and sits inside the plural dogs; the question mark flags the whimsy of dogs holding unpaid bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious means strange or peculiar, the same as odd.

clue.text: GP's motto: "I'm not bothered!"

definitions.meaning: a family doctor looks after every patient, so the phrase read literally is a doctor's creed
a dismissive phrase saying the speaker does not mind at all

explanation.surface: A doctor's slogan turns out to be one of complete indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a general practitioner, the British family doctor. Read literally the phrase means a doctor cares for everyone; as an idiom it means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses indifference, while its literal words describe a doctor treating every patient.

clue.text: Blue being cancelled, look embarrassed

parts.note: an event that is off has been cancelled
to colour is to blush

explanation.surface: A sad person whose event is called off looks embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like sad, but it means risqué or smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-colour jokes are slightly indecent, the same as blue humour.

clue.text: Cleaner departs, pounds removed from overcoat

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

indicators.note: removed from means the letter is taken out of the coat

parts.note: an ulster is a long, loose overcoat
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: The cleaner leaves, having taken the money out of her coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes L out of ULSTER, leaving USTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A duster is a cloth used for cleaning furniture of dust.

clue.text: Hurting after exercise is excellent

indicators.note: after means the aching word follows the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school
achy means aching or hurting

explanation.surface: Being sore after a workout is a fine thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the hurting word behind the school abbreviation for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is informal for very good or fine.

clue.text: Attend to Antony and learn English, free

indicators.note: free here means let loose, so these letters can be set in a new order

explanation.surface: Pay attention to Antony and learn English for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges AND + LEARN + E. In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Mark Antony begins his speech 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to listen, which is what Mark Antony's famous speech asks the crowd to do.

clue.text: Coat back-to-front of no benefit for William

indicators.note: back-to-front means the word for coat is read the other way round

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
U/S, short for unserviceable, is British slang for useless

explanation.surface: A coat worn the wrong way round does William no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' turns FUR into RUF. U/S (unserviceable) is a British way of saying something is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: William II of England, son of the Conqueror, was nicknamed Rufus, probably for his red face or hair.

clue.text: Polish girls here — Hogwarts?

definitions.meaning: a finishing school where young women are given social polish and good manners
the wizarding school in the Harry Potter books, where pupils learn spells and charms

explanation.surface: Girls from Poland attend Harry Potter's school of magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb: to refine. Hogwarts is literally a school of charms, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm schools taught deportment and etiquette to young women; Hogwarts teaches magic charms, giving a punning second sense.

clue.text: Sadly no bar stops robber, one regularly at his peak?

indicators.note: stops means the jumbled letters plug the inside of the word for a robber

parts.note: a mugger is a street robber

indicators.note: sadly means things have gone badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, a bar fails to stop a robber, who often reaches his best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges NO BAR into NROBA, and 'stops' puts it in MUGGER. A Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Munro-bagger aims to climb every Munro, so is often to be found on a summit.

clue.text: Formally, I triumphed in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is taken as spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: to triumph is to have won

explanation.surface: Someone boasts in a formal speech about their victory.
explanation.walkthrough: WON and the answer sound alike. In formal English one may say 'one' in place of 'I', as in 'one does one's best'.
explanation.definitionFit: The impersonal pronoun stands in for the first person in stiff, formal speech.

clue.text: Travel with new leader for military sport

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: travel is a journey

explanation.surface: A trip is undertaken with a new commander for some military games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new leader' replaces the J of JOURNEY with T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourney is a medieval tournament, where knights fought in mock combat as martial sport.

clue.text: No end of stress good for junior

indicators.note: no end of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to underline something is to stress it

explanation.surface: A boss sees endless stress as good for the junior staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' cuts the final E from UNDERLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An underling is a subordinate, someone junior in rank.

clue.text: Bung soldier back into hazardous situation

indicators.note: into means the reversed soldier is placed inside the word for a tight situation

parts.note: a tight spot is a hazardous situation

indicators.note: back means the soldier's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A bribe sends a soldier back into danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the soldier and 'into' places him in the tight situation. 'Bung' looks like slang for a bribe, but here it is a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small peg or plug used to stop the vent of a cask.

clue.text: Not becoming popular, appreciate possessing brother

indicators.note: possessing means the pair holds the brother inside

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to dig something is slang for liking it
Fra is the title of an Italian friar, brother

explanation.surface: It is not becoming to like a brother just because he is popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessing' has the popular word and the slang verb for appreciate hold the friar's title between them. The phrase is Latin, infra dignitatem.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig means beneath one's dignity, so unbecoming.

clue.text: Touch judge officiating at the start in a row

indicators.note: in means those first letters go inside the phrase for a row

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din

indicators.note: at the start means only the opening letter of each of the two words is used

explanation.surface: The judge presiding at the start of a quarrel has to step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' takes the first letters of 'judge officiating', and 'in' places them inside 'a row'. 'Row' is a noisy quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoin are next to each other and touch at a boundary.

clue.text: Precocious girl's speed in swimming Tyne

definitions.note: the possessive ending stands for 'is', a link, leaving the noun

indicators.note: in means the speed abbreviation goes inside the jumbled letters
swimming means the letters are moving about

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A precocious girl races at speed while swimming in the River Tyne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges the river's letters, and 'in' places the speed unit among them. The Tyne is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymphet is a sexually precocious young girl, a word made famous by Nabokov's Lolita.

clue.text: Grey in mountain range? Shame

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the word for a mountain range

parts.note: a chain of mountains is a range

explanation.surface: Grey weather in the mountains is a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the colour abbreviation inside the range; Chambers lists gr. as short for grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is mortification or vexation, the feeling of shame at one's own failure.

clue.text: Poor card game — lead is clubs

indicators.note: lead means the front position, so the suit's letter goes first

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: A bad hand at cards: the lead is a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead is' puts C in front of RUMMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or of low quality.

clue.text: Put on in layers

definitions.meaning: a play that is put on has been produced in a theatre

explanation.surface: Clothes are put on in layers.
explanation.definitionFit: A play mounted for an audience was produced; something built in tiers was done in stages.

clue.text: One stolen by Knave almost, or Jack

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the Knave of Hearts stole the tarts

explanation.surface: A sailor is nearly robbed by a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last T of TART. Both Jack and the answer are old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar and tar are both slang names for a seaman.

clue.text: Out on a limb, raced our military transport

parts.note: an arm is a limb

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking a big risk, we drove our army vehicle fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out on a limb' reads as the idiom for being exposed, but 'Out' rearranges RACED OUR and 'a limb' is ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured car is an armour-plated wheeled vehicle used by the military.

clue.text: Chestnut, I claim regularly, is hot to eat

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for chestnut as a horse's colour

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: I say roast chestnuts are hot to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ILI from 'I claim'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chili peppers are fiery hot, eaten as a spice.

clue.text: In cricket, Edgbaston's principal scorer

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for a cricket

parts.note: a grig is an old word for a cricket or grasshopper

indicators.note: principal means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: At a cricket match, Edgbaston's leading run-scorer is named.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgbaston is a Test cricket ground in Birmingham. The 'cricket' is the insect, GRIG, and 'principal' gives the E that goes in it. A scorer is a composer of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Grieg was a Norwegian composer, someone who writes musical scores.

clue.text: We are very busy, also housing relatives

parts.note: a place that hums is full of busy activity

indicators.note: housing means holding the relatives inside

parts.note: and means also
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: We are rushed off our feet, putting up the family as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' puts the relatives inside the word for also. 'We' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition: all of us people.
explanation.definitionFit: The human race taken as a whole is everyone, so a collective pronoun for us all fits.

clue.text: By leaving close trap

indicators.note: leaving means that letter goes away from the word

parts.note: next means nearest, close by
X, the multiplication sign, is read as 'by', as in three by four

explanation.surface: A trap is shut by someone going away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes X out of NEXT.
explanation.definitionFit: A net is a mesh used to catch fish or animals.

clue.text: Computer experts' jibe: after a period, reject it

definitions.note: the possessive ending is a link, standing for 'is' or 'make'

indicators.note: after means the period comes after the jibe

parts.note: a dig is a jibe or sly remark
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: to reject is to turn back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A jibe aimed at tech experts: after a while, dismiss the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The digerati are people skilled with or knowledgeable about computers and the internet, a play on literati.

clue.text: Way to circle tier

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Instructions for going round a tier of seating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tier' looks like a row or layer, but it means something that ties.
explanation.definitionFit: String is used to tie things up, so it is literally one that ties.
